text:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] rolling firmware job fw-roll-4123 hit repeated serial console resets on rack-usw2-r4 (hosts: gw-usw2-48..55). step 4/10, pausing auto-advancement.
michelle: seeing the same. serial logs spam "pty0: hang" and kvm jumps. provisioning queue for GPU pools in us-west2 is backing up.
raj: tagging @michelle @sam — are we seeing secure boot state flips after the flash?
sam: logs show UEFI variable writes. some nodes flipped SecureBoot=1 briefly, then reverted. not universal. attaching snippet.
pranav: can you paste the exact firmware image and checksum? I want to compare against the golden image we validated in staging.
michelle: image: rb-fw-2026-03-18-v2.bin sha256: 9f8c3a... (truncated). staging run looked fine for < 6h, but production traffic patterns differ (higher long-running KV cache loads).
raj: provisioning backlog: ~120 pending GPU allocations across two controller queues; cost creep obvious if we keep rerunning retries.
sam: quick mitigation: pausing rollout for racks with >1 failure, disable auto-retry on the fleet provisioner. rolling back risky hosts to previous firmware image rb-fw-2026-02-27.
michelle: agreed. initiating a staged rollback for racks r3..r6 in usw2, and gating further steps with manual approval.
pranav: note — runtime KV cache persistence uses u32 offsets that our new boot path touches; on some kernels that triggers tty handshake timeouts. Could be timing-related with NVMe init.
raj: ops-bot, please annotate incident and runbook pointers.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-92. Runbook: infra/firmware -> "firmware-rollback-guidance". Pagerduty alerted to oncall schedule.
sam: temporary policy: for any firmware job touching ACPI/NVMe tables, require one extra canary host with real GPU load (not just smoke).
michelle: rolling a canary reset on gw-usw2-48 (single host) now, will monitor serial for 15m.
pranav: if canary ok, we can re-run with conservative timing (inter-host delay 15m -> 60m) and disable secure-boot flag toggle in the firmware flasher.
raj: cost note: if we let the retry storm continue we'll auto-scale more burst GPUs to satisfy allocs; forecast +18% cost next 12h. Finance aware?
sam: pinging @finance-signal. but primary is availability.
michelle: canary passed: no secure boot flips and serial stable for 18m. but two other hosts still flaky after rollback. collecting dmesg + serial dumps.
pranav: I'll add runtime guard to ignore transient UEFI variable writes during boot window until we have a kernel patch. quick patch idea: hold serial console at 115200 with hwflow disabled to avoid throttle-induced resets.
raj: action items: (1) pause fw-roll-4123 globally; (2) rollback failed hosts to rb-fw-2026-02-27; (3) add canary requirement and increase inter-host delay; (4) runtime guard to tolerate transient UEFI writes; (5) finance notified.
sam: I'll file the change for the fleet orchestrator to enforce the canary+delay. michelle please coordinate the rollback. pranaV? (typo) prAnav? :)
pranav: ha, prAnav here :) I'm on the runtime guard PR now — will tag you for review.
michelle: rollback started. keeping this thread as single source of truth. will post status updates every 30m.
raj: thanks all. if things look unstable after rollback, we escalate to model infra and consider routing traffic to eu-west as temporary capacity relief.
michelle: noted — preparing routing playbook in case we need cross-region spill.
ops-bot: INC-2026-0318-92 updated: severity MED, impact: provisioning delays in us-west2, cost risk flagged.
sam: moving to #eng-oncall for extended triage after next update.
michelle: update @everyone: at +90m rollback complete on 7/8 failed hosts, one node needs hardware-assisted reflash with vendor tool, arranging replace/repair. provisioning queue dropped to 12 pending.
raj: closing immediate incident actions. create a follow-up to root-cause (firmware boot timing + NVMe init interplay).
pranav: will include suggested kernel workarounds and runtime patches in the RCA.
michelle: thanks team, marking this thread closed for now, will link RCA when ready. :thumbsup:
